ambiguities.evidence: Lemma 4 explicitly assumes only absence of underflow errors within FourSumThreeProduct, while the preceding TwoProduct contract requires neither underflow nor overflow and the proof's scaling sentence again says 'provided overflow and underflow do not occur.' (PDF p. 13, printed p. 395, TwoProduct description; PDF p. 14, printed p. 396, Lemma 4 and proof)
ambiguities.impact: A formal contract must at least assume exact TwoProduct decompositions and exclude any range event invalidating them; whether no-overflow is implicit in Lemma 4 or omitted from its statement is not resolved. (PDF p. 13, printed p. 395, TwoProduct description; PDF p. 14, printed p. 396, Lemma 4 proof)
ambiguities.issue: The range-condition wording is not fully uniform about overflow. (PDF p. 13, printed p. 395, TwoProduct description; PDF p. 14, printed p. 396, Lemma 4)

ambiguities.evidence: The lemma uses 'underflow errors,' whereas the proof later uses the broader phrase 'provided overflow and underflow do not occur.' (PDF p. 14, printed p. 396, Lemma 4 and beginning of proof)
ambiguities.impact: The source clearly excludes inexact underflow affecting the four-term transformation, but its wording does not unambiguously classify exact operations in the underflow range. (PDF p. 14, printed p. 396, Lemma 4)
ambiguities.issue: The phrase 'absence of underflow errors' does not explicitly say whether exact subnormal operations are allowed. (PDF p. 14, printed p. 396, Lemma 4)

ambiguities.evidence: The paper identifies TwoProduct as a known algorithm and supplies its semantic contract, including equation (17), rather than listing its operations. (PDF p. 13, printed p. 395, TwoProduct description; PDF p. 14, printed p. 396, eq. (17))
ambiguities.impact: Faithfulness to Lemma 4 depends on preserving the exact high-plus-low TwoProduct contract, not on selecting an unstated implementation. (PDF p. 14, printed p. 396, eq. (17) and FourSumThreeProduct linkage)
ambiguities.issue: The internal implementation of TwoProduct is not reproduced. (PDF p. 13, printed p. 395, TwoProduct description)

contract_plain_english: ThreeProduct applies three exact TwoProduct decompositions, merges the two middle terms with an error-free FastTwoSum call, and adds that merge's residual to the fourth term without rounding error. Subject to the stated range assumptions, its three floating-point outputs form an exact unevaluated representation of x1 x2 x3 for arbitrary base beta. (PDF p. 13, printed p. 395, FourSumThreeProduct; PDF p. 14, printed p. 396, Lemma 4 and eq. (18); PDF p. 15, printed p. 397, proof conclusion)

source_evidence.anchor: Section 4.2, FourSumThreeProduct algorithm and TwoProduct description
source_evidence.observation: FourSumThreeProduct performs three TwoProduct calls and produces four terms; the paper states that TwoProduct is error-free if neither underflow nor overflow occurs.

source_evidence.anchor: Equation (17), ThreeProduct algorithm, and Lemma 4 equation (18)
source_evidence.observation: Equation (17) gives the exact high-plus-low decomposition for the first product, ThreeProduct merges the two middle terms with FastTwoSum, and Lemma 4 states that its three outputs sum exactly to the product of its three inputs.

source_evidence.anchor: Lemma 4 proof, FastTwoSum merge and final exact addition
source_evidence.observation: The proof verifies condition (7) for the middle-term merge, obtains s2+s3''=s2'+s3', and proves that s3''+s4' lies in F and is added without error.
The cross-referenced theorem supplies the base-independent FastTwoSum error-free identity once condition (7) holds.

statement.algorithm_linkage: The claim is specifically for ThreeProduct: three TwoProduct calls create the standard four-term expansion, FastTwoSum merges s2' and s3' into s2 and its exact residual s3'', and one final floating-point addition merges s3'' with s4'. (PDF p. 13, printed p. 395, FourSumThreeProduct; PDF p. 14, printed p. 396, ThreeProduct; PDF p. 15, printed p. 397, proof conclusion)
binders: For every triple of scalar inputs x1,x2,x3 in F satisfying the range assumptions, run ThreeProduct and denote its floating-point outputs by s1,s2,s3. (PDF p. 14, printed p. 396, ThreeProduct algorithm and Lemma 4)

Let t_h,t_l,s2',s3',s4',s3'' denote the intermediate outputs of the nested TwoProduct and FastTwoSum calls shown by FourSumThreeProduct and ThreeProduct. (PDF p. 13, printed p. 395, FourSumThreeProduct algorithm; PDF p. 14, printed p. 396, ThreeProduct algorithm)
conclusions: The three returned floating-point terms satisfy the exact real identity s1+s2+s3=x1 x2 x3. (PDF p. 14, printed p. 396, Lemma 4 and eq. (18))
The FastTwoSum merge is error-free: s2+s3''=s2'+s3'. (PDF p. 15, printed p. 397, equation following verification of condition (7))
The final computed addition is also exact: s3=s3''+s4'. (PDF p. 15, printed p. 397, final sentence of Lemma 4 proof)

Consequently, the four-term exact expansion from FourSumThreeProduct is reduced to an exact three-term unevaluated sum. (PDF p. 14, printed p. 396, discussion preceding ThreeProduct; PDF p. 15, printed p. 397, proof conclusion)

The middle-term FastTwoSum call requires no restriction beta in {2,3}, because condition (7) is established directly. (PDF p. 14, printed p. 396, paragraph preceding ThreeProduct; PDF p. 15, printed p. 397, condition-(7) calculation)
constants_and_indexing: Equation (18) sums output indices i=1,2,3 and multiplies input indices i=1,2,3; the earlier four-term expansion uses s1 plus s_i' for i=2,3,4. (PDF p. 14, printed p. 396, eq. (18) and preceding discussion)
The TwoProduct low-part bound has the exact factor 1/2: |t_l|≤(1/2) ulp(x2 x3). (PDF p. 14, printed p. 396, eq. (17))
The middle-term proof establishes |s3'|≤(1/2) beta^p beta^{e(s2')}≤(beta^p-beta/2) beta^{e(s2')}, exactly matching condition (7). (PDF p. 15, printed p. 397, condition-(7) calculation)
After proof normalization, |s3''|≤(1/2) beta^p and |s4'|≤(1/2) beta^p, hence |s3''+s4'|≤beta^p and the integer sum lies in F. (PDF p. 15, printed p. 397, final bounds)
definitions_and_conventions: FourSumThreeProduct computes (t_h,t_l)=TwoProduct(x2,x3), (s1,s2')=TwoProduct(x1,t_h), and (s3',s4')=TwoProduct(x1,t_l). (PDF p. 13, printed p. 395, FourSumThreeProduct algorithm)

For the first TwoProduct call, t_h+t_l=x2 x3 exactly, t_h is the computed rounded product x2⊗x3, and |t_l|≤(1/2) ulp(x2 x3); the other two calls use the corresponding exact high-plus-low contracts. (PDF p. 14, printed p. 396, eq. (17) and following sentence)
ThreeProduct first obtains the four terms, then computes (s2,s3'')=FastTwoSum(s2',s3'), and finally computes s3=s3''⊕s4'. (PDF p. 14, printed p. 396, ThreeProduct algorithm)
The right side x1 x2 x3 in equation (18) is the exact real product, while the s_i are computed floating-point values whose unevaluated real sum is taken. (PDF p. 14, printed p. 396, eq. (18))
error_notions: The final property is error-free transformation, not a small-error approximation: the output sum equals the exact triple product. (PDF p. 14, printed p. 396, eq. (18))

Intermediate low terms are exact signed residuals of their corresponding TwoProduct or FastTwoSum operations. (PDF p. 14, printed p. 396, eq. (17) and ThreeProduct line 2; PDF p. 15, printed p. 397, exact merge identity)

The ulp estimates in the proof establish representability and exactness; they are not residual error terms left in equation (18). (PDF p. 14, printed p. 396, proof bounds; PDF p. 15, printed p. 397, proof conclusion)
exceptional_values: The explicit lemma condition concerns underflow errors in FourSumThreeProduct. (PDF p. 14, printed p. 396, Lemma 4)

The preceding TwoProduct description and the scaling sentence in the proof additionally refer to absence of both underflow and overflow. (PDF p. 13, printed p. 395, TwoProduct description; PDF p. 14, printed p. 396, beginning of proof)
The case x1 x2 x3=0 is explicitly treated as trivial rather than excluded. (PDF p. 14, printed p. 396, beginning of proof)
The model F contains finite real values and does not model NaNs or infinities. (PDF p. 2, printed p. 384, eq. (1))
higher_order_terms: Equation (18) is exact and contains no big-O term, omitted product term, or higher-order remainder. (PDF p. 14, printed p. 396, eq. (18))
hypotheses: Lemma 4 explicitly assumes the absence of underflow errors within the FourSumThreeProduct call. (PDF p. 14, printed p. 396, Lemma 4)

The inherited TwoProduct contract used for the four-term expansion is error-free when neither underflow nor overflow occurs. (PDF p. 13, printed p. 395, TwoProduct description; PDF p. 14, printed p. 396, eq. (17))

The middle inputs s2',s3' are proved to satisfy Theorem 2 condition (7); this is a derived fact, not an ordering hypothesis imposed on x1,x2,x3. (PDF p. 14, printed p. 396, paragraph before ThreeProduct; PDF p. 15, printed p. 397, condition-(7) calculation)
implicit_context: Unless stated otherwise, operations on F are rounded to nearest; this standing convention applies to the displayed multiplication and addition operations. (PDF p. 2, printed p. 384, standing rounding convention; PDF p. 14, printed p. 396, algorithms)
Neither |s2'|≥|s3'| nor ulp(s2')≥ulp(s3') is assumed or generally true; the proof instead establishes condition (7). (PDF p. 14, printed p. 396, paragraph preceding ThreeProduct)

For the proof, the zero-product case is declared trivial and the nonzero case is rescaled by powers of beta so that ulp(x_i)=1 and |x_i|≤beta^p-1; this is a proof normalization, not an additional input-format requirement. (PDF p. 14, printed p. 396, beginning of Lemma 4 proof)
norms: All intermediate bounds use scalar absolute value and ulp; equation (18) is a scalar algebraic identity, with no vector or matrix norm. (PDF p. 14, printed p. 396, eqs. (17)-(18); PDF p. 15, printed p. 397, proof bounds)
numerical_model: TwoProduct supplies exact high-plus-low decompositions under its stated range assumptions, with the high part obtained by floating-point multiplication. (PDF p. 13, printed p. 395, TwoProduct description; PDF p. 14, printed p. 396, eq. (17))

FastTwoSum is applied to s2',s3' under Theorem 2's condition (7), rather than under absolute-value or ulp ordering. (PDF p. 14, printed p. 396, paragraph before ThreeProduct; PDF p. 15, printed p. 397, condition-(7) calculation)

The last operation is written as a rounded addition, but the proof establishes representability of its exact result, so no rounding error occurs. (PDF p. 14, printed p. 396, ThreeProduct line 3; PDF p. 15, printed p. 397, final bound)
No restriction to binary or ternary bases is imposed on the ThreeProduct merge. (PDF p. 14, printed p. 396, paragraph before ThreeProduct)

undebatable_constraints: There are exactly three floating-point inputs and three returned floating-point terms. (PDF p. 14, printed p. 396, ThreeProduct algorithm)
The exact conclusion is a sum-to-product identity, s1+s2+s3=x1 x2 x3, not a statement that any individual s_i equals the full product. (PDF p. 14, printed p. 396, eq. (18))
The source first forms the four-term expansion with three TwoProduct calls. (PDF p. 13, printed p. 395, FourSumThreeProduct algorithm)
The source merges s2' and s3' with FastTwoSum and then merges its residual with s4'. (PDF p. 14, printed p. 396, ThreeProduct lines 2-3)
The middle FastTwoSum transformation and the final addition are both exact. (PDF p. 15, printed p. 397, exact merge identity and final sentence)
No hypotheses |s2'|≥|s3'| or ulp(s2')≥ulp(s3') may be added. (PDF p. 14, printed p. 396, paragraph preceding ThreeProduct)
The lemma does not state uniqueness, ordering, nonoverlap, or a rounded-full-product property for the three output components. (PDF p. 14, printed p. 396, Lemma 4 and eq. (18))
The exact identity has no fourth residual term. (PDF p. 14, printed p. 396, eq. (18); PDF p. 15, printed p. 397, proof conclusion)
